name: Hemoglobin E-beta-thalassemia major

criteria.description: Identification of compound heterozygosity for hemoglobin E mutation and beta-thalassemia mutation by molecular genetic testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing elevated Hb E and reduced or absent Hb A
Presence of transfusion-dependent anemia with clinical features consistent with thalassemia major
Bone marrow showing erythroid hyperplasia and ineffective erythropoiesis
Family history of hemoglobin E or beta-thalassemia trait

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of compound heterozygosity confirmed by genetic testing plus clinical evidence of transfusion-dependent anemia and hemoglobin electrophoresis consistent with Hb E-beta-thalassemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of genetic, hematologic, and clinical data.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic anemia refractory to iron therapy

laboratory: Microcytic hypochromic anemia with low hemoglobin and hematocrit
Elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation indicating iron overload
Peripheral blood smear showing target cells and nucleated red blood cells
imaging: X-ray showing marrow expansion with cortical thinning and bone deformities
MRI T2* for quantification of cardiac and hepatic iron overload
other: Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing elevated Hb E (25-40%) and reduced or absent Hb A
Bone marrow biopsy showing erythroid hyperplasia and ineffective erythropoiesis

distinguishingFeatures: Different hemoglobin electrophoresis pattern with absent Hb E
More severe anemia onset in infancy
Normal or mildly abnormal hemoglobin electrophoresis
Low serum ferritin and iron studies consistent with deficiency
No genetic mutations in HBB gene

redFlags: Severe transfusion-dependent anemia presenting in early childhood
Signs of iron overload such as cardiac dysfunction or endocrine abnormalities
